chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abi al-Mi'za from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Ibn Abi Ya'fur from Mu'alla ibn Khunays from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'What is the meaning of the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "Indeed, Allah commands you to render the trusts to those to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice."'
Indeed, Allah commands you to render the trusts to those to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice.
He (peace be upon him) said, 'It is upon the Imam to return what is with him to the Imam who comes after him. The Imams were commanded to be just, and the people were commanded to follow them.'

key_terms.الْأَمَانَاتِ: trusts (plural of amanah, referring to authority, knowledge, or property)
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ الَّذِي بَعْدَهُ: the Imam who comes after him

ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars interpret the command to 'render trusts' in relation to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the specific duty of the Imams to transfer the 'trust' (authority and knowledge) to their successor and the general obligation of justice upon them, which necessitates the people's obedience. This exegesis underscores the concept of *Nass* (designation) and the continuity of divine authority, linking the political and spiritual leadership directly to the Quranic command of returning trusts. It highlights that while the people are commanded to follow the Imams in justice, the Imams themselves bear the unique responsibility of maintaining the chain of succession.
